how_to_use: Look up years[<year>]. Draw each entry of 'causes' as a map marker at 'pos' (inside the map) using 'icon' and 'color'; show 'label', 'value' and 'text' on hover. Show 'why', 'outcome', 'people_text' and 'events' as text. Levels run from -2 (pushes towards a small flood) to +2 (pushes towards a large flood).

sources.headwater_rain: ERA5 reanalysis via Open-Meteo, mean of three points in the Angolan highlands, November-April total
sources.inflow: GloFAS river discharge reanalysis via Open-Meteo, peak monthly mean January-June. A MODEL, not a gauge.
sources.local_rain: ERA5 reanalysis via Open-Meteo at -19.3, 22.9, November-April total
sources.heat: NASA POWER (MERRA-2) daily maximum temperature, May-October mean
sources.enso: NOAA Climate Prediction Center, Oceanic Nino Index, December-February
sources.people: WorldPop 2020, 1 km, UN-adjusted (CC BY 4.0), counted within 5 km of that year's Landsat open water

caveats: Causes are associations, not proof: a year can be wet for reasons not listed here, and last year's water carries over.
River inflow is a hydrological model. It disagrees with the mapped water in some years (for example 2025).
Population is held at its 2020 distribution in every year, so the change between years comes from the water, not from growth. Living near water is not the same as being flooded or helped.
Events are from news reports and a travel guide; they are illustrations, not a complete record.

events.title: Floods displace families
events.text: Floods on the Okavango, Zambezi and Chobe displaced 430 people and submerged eight villages. In Ngamiland 61 hectares of ploughed fields went under water and lodges at Sepopa were flooded.

events.title: Largest floods in recent memory
events.text: Between 2010 and 2012 the Delta saw some of its largest floods in recent memory; channels and lagoons dry for decades refilled and water reached Lake Ngami.
events.source: okavango.com (travel guide, not a scientific source)

events.title: The flood did not arrive
events.text: Water sources across Ngamiland dried up, leaving communities, livestock and wildlife in a dire situation. Fishermen and mokoro polers lost their income and farmers lost cattle.

events.title: The Delta springs back to life
events.text: The flood returned and was expected to reach the Thamalakane River at Maun in mid-May, restoring water for farming, fishing and mokoro tourism.
